A big release: share several files under one link, preview images / video / audio / text / PDF before downloading, optionally lock uploads, and revoke shares early. Everything stays zero-knowledge — the server only ever stores opaque ciphertext.

## Added

- **Multi-file shares.** Select or drop several files at once; they upload as one end-to-end-encrypted bundle under a single link, and the recipient gets the original files back individually (no zip). The download page lists them with **Download all** and, on Chromium over HTTPS, **Save to folder**.
- **Inline preview before download.** View **images** (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO, APNG, and SVG rendered safely via `<img>`), **video** (MP4, WebM, OGG, MOV, M4V), **audio** (MP3, M4A/AAC, OGG, WAV, FLAC, Opus), **text & code**, and **PDF** right on the share page. Decryption is client-side and previewing never costs an extra download. Large videos stream progressively through the service worker; other kinds are size-capped to keep memory bounded, and only inert types render (no SVG/HTML scripting).
- **Optional upload protection.** Set `UPLOAD_PASSWORD` and only people who know it can create shares; download links stay open to everyone. Enforced server-side (constant-time, rejected before anything is stored). Unset = open, exactly as before.
- **Per-share management link.** Every new share comes with a secret link (`/m/<slug>#t=…`, shown next to the share link) that lets you delete it before it expires. The server stores only a hash of the token; the token lives in the URL fragment.

## Notes

- Zero-knowledge throughout: the server never sees file contents, names, types, counts, keys, or tokens — only opaque blobs and hashes.
- Single-file shares and links created by earlier versions keep working unchanged.
- Streaming video preview plays progressively; seeking far into a very large video re-decrypts from the start (inherent to the sequential encryption). A fully seekable format is a possible future step.
- `UPLOAD_PASSWORD` is available in the Unraid template (advanced); use a value without leading/trailing spaces.
